lingual-braces.summary: Braces bonded to the back of your teeth that straighten your smile without visible brackets, with more tongue and speech adjustment than outer braces.

quick.overview:
Lingual braces are fixed braces attached to the tongue side of the teeth, so your smile looks like it has no hardware while the teeth move into alignment. They were first developed in California in the mid-1970s.

Brackets and wires on the inner surfaces apply steady forces that move teeth, the same principle as braces on the outer surfaces. A 2016 systematic review reports more tongue pain, speech and eating difficulty and harder cleaning than with outer braces. Forum posters also ask whether braces change facial structure, a question with little direct research.
quick.how: Treatment is delivered by an orthodontist, who bonds custom brackets to the inner tooth surfaces and adjusts the wires at regular visits. People wear them for the length of a normal orthodontic course, often with a short period of adapting to speech and eating, and brush and clean around the brackets carefully.
quick.risks: Compared with outer braces, lingual braces are linked to more tongue pain, speech and eating difficulty and harder cleaning; brackets break more often in some designs, and finishing the bite can be harder. White spot lesions on enamel can still occur with poor hygiene.

angle.text: People choose lingual braces to straighten their teeth without brackets showing on the front surfaces, so the smile looks better while treatment is under way. Tooth movement by braces is well studied; claims that braces or extractions reshape the face come from forum anecdote.

miswak-chew-stick.summary: A traditional twig toothbrush from the arak tree used for cleaner, fresher, brighter-looking teeth; small trials report less plaque.

quick.overview:
Miswak is a chewing stick cut from the Salvadora persica tree, used for centuries in the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. The frayed end works as a natural brush, and people use it for cleaner teeth, fresher breath and, in traditional accounts, a whiter, polished look.

The fibres scrub plaque off the teeth, and plant compounds such as benzyl isothiocyanate have shown antibacterial activity in laboratory tests. Reviews report reductions in plaque and gum inflammation in small trials; those trials measure plaque and gum health, not tooth colour.
quick.how: You chew or peel one end to expose the fibres, then rub them over the teeth, often after meals or alongside a regular toothbrush. Users value it as a cheap, portable cleaner and trim the frayed end as it wears down.
quick.risks: Reviews describe it as low-risk and cheap, with variable study quality and a call for larger trials. Comparisons cited on Wikipedia show lower antibacterial activity than chlorhexidine, and a dental-journal letter discusses misuse of the stick.

angle.text: Miswak is used as a natural toothbrush so teeth look cleaner and brighter. The stick scrubs off plaque and stain, and small trials have measured less plaque; tooth colour itself has not been tested.

colored-circle-contact-lenses.summary: Tinted or ring-edged contact lenses that change eye colour or make the iris look larger; the FDA treats them as prescription medical devices.

quick.overview:
Coloured and circle lenses are cosmetic contacts that change the look of your iris, either by tinting it or by adding a ring that makes the eye appear larger. In forums they are mostly used to lighten dark eyes, and the change shows the moment they go in.

A printed pigment layer covers or modifies the natural iris colour, and circle lenses add a darker or larger outer rim to enlarge the visible iris. No studies were found that measure how much they change perceived attractiveness, so that part rests on user reports.
quick.how: People get fitted by an eye-care professional, then wear them for the day like regular contacts, choosing a shade or diameter for a natural or dramatic look. Forum users compare shades, wear time and how natural the result looks.
quick.risks: The FDA classes decorative lenses as medical devices needing a prescription and lists corneal abrasion, allergy, reduced vision and infection that can lead to blindness, especially from lenses obtained without a proper fitting. A case report notes that some circle lenses contain metals that can matter during MRI.

angle.text: Coloured lenses lighten or change eye colour and circle lenses make the iris look bigger, with the effect visible as soon as they are worn. How much this adds to overall attractiveness is a matter of forum opinion rather than studies.

foot-orthotic-insoles.summary: Shoe inserts for comfort, arch support and, in some products, extra height; studied for heel pain rather than posture or looks.

quick.overview:
Orthotic insoles are removable supports for the shoe, either custom made from a foot scan or bought ready made. They are sold for comfort, arch support, pain relief and, in some products, extra height of a small amount, with people hoping for steadier standing and a more upright stance.

They redistribute load across the foot and may hold the arch or heel in a set position, and heel inserts raise the heel a little. Their best-studied use is heel pain from plantar fasciitis; no studies were found of them for posture, gait appearance or height in people without a foot problem.
quick.how: People slip them into everyday or athletic shoes, either a ready-made pair or a custom pair made from a cast or scan. Height-oriented inserts are worn like lifts inside the shoe and need enough shoe room to fit.
quick.risks: Reviews describe mixed evidence for medical use and inconsistent fit across methods. No harms of insoles themselves were identified in the sources reviewed; clinicians treat underlying foot conditions with several measures, not insoles alone.

angle.text: Some insoles add measurable height while worn, and others are used for comfort and arch support that people hope will help their stance. Trials have studied them for heel pain; effects on posture and looks have not been tested.

gynecomastia-compression-vest.summary: A tight undershirt that flattens the chest so male breast tissue shows less under clothes; it conceals rather than treats.

quick.overview:
A gynecomastia compression vest is an elastic undershirt that presses the chest flat so enlarged male breast tissue shows less through clothing. The flatter outline is visible straight away, and the tissue underneath does not change.

Pressure from the elastic fabric holds the chest tissue against the body, which changes the outline under a shirt. Gynecomastia is common in adolescence, and most teenage cases resolve within about two years; no studies were found that test compression garments for it.
quick.how: Men wear the vest as a base layer under shirts through the day or for particular occasions, picking a snug size that stays flat without feeling restrictive. It is often used while waiting on other approaches such as observation, medication or surgery.
quick.risks: No published safety data for these vests were found. Medical sources describe observation, medication and surgery as management routes for persistent gynecomastia, and note that causes such as drugs or illness are evaluated by clinicians.

angle.text: Men wear compression vests to flatten the chest so gynecomastia is less visible under shirts, with the change showing immediately. The vest conceals rather than treats the tissue, and no studies test it.

spray-tan-booth.summary: An automated booth that mists DHA onto your skin for an even, UV-free tan that fades over about a week.

quick.overview:
A spray-tan booth coats your body in a mist of dihydroxyacetone (DHA), which turns the outer skin layer brown without UV light, giving an even bronzed colour visible within hours. The colour fades over about 5 to 10 days.

DHA reacts with amino acids in dead surface skin cells in a Maillard-type browning reaction, and the colour fades as those cells shed. The tanning effect itself is well described; the effect of breathing the mist has not been tested in people.
quick.how: People book a session at a salon, often before an event or a photo shoot, and repeat when the colour fades. Protective items such as eye and lip coverings are commonly used, and the tan is often paired with moisturizing to keep it even.
quick.risks: The FDA has approved DHA for external use only, not for the eyes, lips, mucous membranes or inhalation, and booth spraying can make that exposure difficult to avoid. Cell and mouse studies report DNA damage, cell stress and lung inflammation; no human trials of booth inhalation were found. Contact dermatitis has been reported.

angle.text: A spray-tan booth gives an even bronzed colour without UV exposure, visible within hours and fading over about a week. The DHA mist darkens the dead outer skin layer; inhaling the mist has not been studied in humans.

bronzer.summary: A wash-off skin tint in powder, lotion or spray form that gives an instant tanned, warmer look with no UV.

quick.overview:
A bronzer is a cosmetic colorant, sold as a powder, lotion, gel, mousse or spray, that tints the skin until it is washed off. People use it for an instant tan look, to even out skin tone, or to add shading to the face and body.

Bronzers deposit colour on the outer surface of the skin; common colourants include walnut extract, jojoba extract and caramel. It differs from a DHA self-tanner, which reacts with the skin for longer-lasting colour, and in bodybuilding it is a colour layer used alongside spray tans on stage.
quick.how: People sweep or blend it onto the face, neck and body for the day, often matching a body tan or adding shading to cheekbones, and wash it off at night with soap and water. It is also worn over a longer-lasting self-tan.
quick.risks: Reported downsides are an orange or patchy look if applied unevenly, transfer onto clothing, and skin reactions in people allergic to ingredients such as fragrances or benzyl alcohol. A bronzer does not tan the skin and is not a sunscreen, and dermatology sources note that sunless products give no meaningful UV protection.

angle.text: Bronzer gives a tanned, warmer complexion the moment it goes on, for the face to match a body tan or to add shading. The colour sits on the skin surface and washes off at the end of the day.

gradual-tanning-lotion.summary: A daily moisturizer with a mild self-tanning agent that builds a natural-looking, streak-resistant colour over several days.

quick.overview:
A gradual tanning lotion is a moisturizer or body lotion containing a small amount of a self-tanning agent, usually dihydroxyacetone (DHA). Used regularly, it deepens skin colour step by step, and a slight change is usually visible after the first application.

Users like it because slow build-up is less likely to leave streaks or an orange cast than a one-off self-tan. DHA is a simple sugar that reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin in a browning reaction; the pigments are not melanin and form without UV light.
quick.how: People apply it like a daily body lotion, often for several days in a row until the shade they want, then continue every day or two to hold it. The colour fades over several days as the outer skin sheds, which is why it is reapplied.
quick.risks: Reported concerns centre on DHA: contact dermatitis, a possible increase in free-radical formation in sun-exposed skin soon after application, and no meaningful UV protection. Regulators approve DHA for external use and not for the eyes, lips or mucous membranes.

angle.text: Gradual tanning lotion builds a natural-looking tan over several days, with a slight colour change usually visible after the first use. The colour deepens with repeated daily application and does not protect against UV.

tanning-accelerator.summary: Lotions or pills, often tyrosine or psoralen based, used alongside UV exposure in the hope of tanning faster and darker.

quick.overview:
Tanning accelerators are lotions (and sometimes pills) marketed to indoor and outdoor tanners to make a tan appear faster or darker. They typically contain the amino acid tyrosine, psoralens or other chemicals, and are meant to be used together with UV exposure.

Marketing holds that tyrosine, a building block of melanin, increases pigment production; encyclopedic sources say no scientific data supports that claim. Psoralens such as 5-methoxypsoralen are photosensitizing compounds used medically in psoriasis and vitiligo, and have also been described as tanning accelerators.
quick.how: People apply the lotion before sun or sunbed sessions, or take pills in the run-up to tanning. A 2015 survey of 200 indoor tanners found just over half used accelerators and that users tended to tan more often.
quick.risks: In the 2015 survey, acne and rashes were more common among users, and adverse reactions stopped further use about 31 percent of the time. Psoralens are photosensitizers, and a rhesus monkey study found a high share of topically applied 5-methoxypsoralen was absorbed. Accelerators are used with UV exposure, a documented cause of skin cancer.

angle.text: Users apply or take tanning accelerators hoping to darken faster and deeper during UV exposure by boosting melanin production. Wikipedia notes no scientific data supports the melanin claim, and survey users report acne and rashes.

upf-clothing.summary: Fabric tested and labelled for how much UV it blocks, worn as a no-reapplication way to limit sun exposure and the skin ageing that follows.

quick.overview:
UPF clothing is made from fabric tested for ultraviolet protection factor, a lab measure of how much sunburn-causing UV passes through the cloth. UPF 50+ is the top published category, rated as blocking at least about 98 percent of UV.

People who want to limit sun-related skin ageing, uneven pigmentation or skin cancer risk wear it over covered areas without applying sunscreen, along with hats and shade. Fabric absorbs, reflects or scatters UV, and laboratory evidence that clothing reduces UV reaching skin is strong; no trial reviewed measured appearance outcomes such as wrinkles.
quick.how: People wear UPF shirts, hats, sleeves and pants for outdoor time and use sunscreen on exposed skin. Denser weave, darker colour, heavier weight and added UV absorbers raise the rating.
quick.risks: The clothing itself carries little risk. Documented limits are reduced protection when wet or stretched, heat retention in heavy dark fabrics, and uncovered skin remaining exposed. Standards in North America are industry-led test methods rather than a government approval.

angle.text: UPF clothing blocks UV from reaching covered skin, which is promoted as a way to limit sun damage, spots and wrinkles over time. The fabric's UV blocking is lab-rated; its effect on visible ageing has not been studied directly.

light-box-sad-lamp.summary: A bright-light lamp used each morning to lift winter mood and steady sleep and energy, which people connect to looking more rested.

quick.overview:
A light box, or SAD lamp, emits up to about 10,000 lux of filtered white light, far above ordinary indoor lighting, and is used by sitting in front of it, usually in the morning. People use it for winter low mood, sleep timing and energy, which they link to looking more rested and fresher.

Bright light is detected by light-sensitive retinal cells that suppress melatonin and help reset the body clock. A 2020 meta-analysis of 19 randomized trials found bright light superior to placebo for seasonal affective disorder; no study has tested light boxes for facial appearance.
quick.how: Users sit near the lamp for a set time in the morning, often while having breakfast or working, through the darker months. Lamps sold online are often weaker than clinic-grade units.
quick.risks: Reported side effects include headache, eye irritation, jumpiness and nausea, and light therapy can trigger mania in people prone to it. Sources list light-sensitive eye conditions, photosensitive skin conditions, porphyria and photosensitizing drugs or herbs as reasons for caution, and recommend clinician supervision.

angle.text: Bright morning light steadies the body clock, mood and energy, which users connect to sleeping better and looking more rested. Trials have studied light boxes for seasonal depression; effects on appearance have not been tested.

mattress-medium-firm.summary: A middle-firmness mattress that sleep research links to less back pain, and that forums link to better sleep and posture.

quick.overview:
A medium-firm mattress balances support and cushioning so the spine stays roughly level. People pick it for comfortable sleep, less back pain and the more rested, upright look they connect to that.

Firmness affects how much the body sinks and how the spine is aligned in lying positions. Sleep and back-pain research, including a 2003 randomized trial, has associated medium-firm beds with less chronic low back pain; no study has tested mattress firmness for facial structure, height or other appearance outcomes.
quick.how: People choose a medium-firm innerspring, foam or hybrid bed and match it to their sleeping position. Wikipedia says firm mattresses are suggested for stomach sleepers and some back sleepers, soft ones for side sleepers, and medium ones for most back sleepers.
quick.risks: A mattress carries little direct risk. Forum users blame soft surfaces that sag under the lower back for back pain, and the sources reviewed do not endorse a very hard surface. Hospital research on pressure injuries uses specialised foam, air and alternating-pressure mattresses rather than home beds.

angle.text: A supportive medium-firm mattress is chosen for less back pain and better sleep, which people connect to a more upright posture and a rested look. Research links it to lower back pain; facial and skeletal effects have not been tested.

home-uvb-booth.summary: A stand-up narrowband UVB phototherapy cabinet designed for home skin treatment, which some users also consider for darkening skin tone.

quick.overview:
A home UVB booth is a full-body cabinet that emits narrowband ultraviolet-B light, typically around 311-313 nm. Dermatology uses this wavelength to treat psoriasis, vitiligo and eczema, and some patients receive treatment at home instead of in a clinic. In tanning circles it comes up as a way to darken skin with mostly UVB rather than the UVA-heavy light of salon sunbeds.

UVB stimulates new melanin production over a few days, whereas UVA mainly darkens melanin already present. Published research on these devices concerns skin disease, including a 2024 trial comparing home and office treatment for psoriasis; there are no trials of a home UVB booth as a tanning tool.
quick.how: In medical use, a clinician prescribes a schedule and the patient stands in the cabinet for timed sessions at home. Tanning use is discussed in forums but has no published protocol.
quick.risks: UV exposure is associated with progressive skin damage, skin cancer, cataracts and burns, and the IARC classifies UV radiation as a Group 1 carcinogen. Photosensitising drugs, some herbs such as St John's wort, porphyria and photosensitive skin conditions are listed as contraindications. Medical use is normally supervised by a clinician, and rules on tanning devices vary by country.

angle.text: Some users look at home UVB booths as a way to build a tan with less UVA than a sunbed, since UVB triggers new melanin production. The cabinets are established for skin conditions such as psoriasis; cosmetic tanning use has not been studied.

concealer-for-men.summary: A pigmented cosmetic dabbed over dark circles, blemishes and redness to even out skin tone straight away.

quick.overview:
Concealer is a thick, highly pigmented makeup used on small areas, most often to mask under-eye dark circles, spots, redness and scars. The evened-out tone shows immediately, and men use it as a quick, low-cost way to look fresher and reduce the look of eye bags.

Its pigment sits on top of the skin and blocks or neutralises the darker or redder tone beneath. Makeup guides describe yellow or peach tones for dark circles, green for redness such as pimples or rosacea, and a shade one or two steps lighter than the skin for brightening. Research on concealer itself is sparse and mostly not specific to men.
quick.how: It comes as liquid, cream, stick, pencil and cream-to-powder, and is blended in with fingers, a brush or a sponge, on its own or over or under foundation. Men discuss using small amounts to keep it discreet.
quick.risks: Concealer is a cosmetic generally sold without prescription. Some products contain ingredients such as fragrance, mineral oil, dimethicone or talc, which can bother sensitive skin. A 2021 questionnaire study of 539 Korean adults examined links between cosmetic use and acne. It covers the look of dark circles and blemishes while worn and does not change their cause.

angle.text: Men use concealer to cover under-eye circles, blemishes and redness, and the evened-out tone is visible straight away. Pigment on the skin blocks the darker or redder colour underneath; male-specific research is limited.

eyebrow-pencil-powder.summary: Pencils and powders that fill sparse or uneven brows with pigment for a fuller, better-defined frame around the eyes.

quick.overview:
Eyebrow pencils and powders are makeup products used to outline, darken or fill in the brows. Pencils draw fine hair-like strokes, while powders, often applied with a small angled brush, give a softer, fuller finish, and the fuller look shows as soon as they are applied.

The products deposit pigment on the skin and hairs, filling gaps and sharpening the outline. Powders are usually matched closely to natural hair colour for a softer look. In grooming discussions they are a way to change brow density or shape without surgery or transplants; published research on the products themselves is limited.
quick.how: People apply them daily, filling sparse spots and tracing the shape, sometimes with a brow gel to set hairs. The effect lasts while worn and is removed with makeup remover.
quick.risks: As ordinary cosmetics they carry the usual risk of skin irritation or allergy to ingredients in some individuals. The sources reviewed contain no studies on adverse effects specific to brow pencils or powders, and the products do not change hair growth.

angle.text: Pencils and powders fill gaps and define brow shape for a fuller look, visible as soon as they are applied. A fuller, defined brow frames the eyes, and the effect lasts while the product is worn.

hair-styling-clay-pomade.summary: Wax-, oil- or clay-based styling products that hold and texture hair into a chosen shape for the day.

quick.overview:
Hair clay and pomade shape and hold hair so a cut looks neat and styled all day. Pomade is traditionally greasy, waxy or water-based and gives a shiny, slick finish; clay is a related styling paste with a more matte, textured look. Both appear in grooming discussions as tools for the pompadour, quiff and textured crop.

Pomades are mostly petroleum jelly, mineral oil or lanolin, often with beeswax for stiffness; water-based versions use polymers and hardening agents. Wax-type products stay pliable and hold hair in place without drying out like alcohol-heavy gels. The evidence base is mostly product descriptions and history, with no clinical studies.
quick.how: People work a small amount through towel-dried or dry hair with the hands or a comb and shape the style, choosing a heavier or lighter hold for the look they want. Oil-based products need repeated washes to remove; water-based ones rinse out more easily.
quick.risks: Wikipedia reports that some styling-product ingredients can strip oils or build up on hair, contributing to dryness, and that petroleum-based pomades can take several washes to remove; claims about follicle clogging or hair loss rest on non-clinical sources. A 2023 measurement study of Beijing hair salons found that styling products including clay, wax and gel release volatile organic compounds.

angle.text: Clay and pomade hold and texture hair so a style keeps its shape, giving a matte or slick finish visible immediately. They are styling aids for a neater, more put-together haircut through the day.

cologne-perfume.summary: Alcohol-based fragrance worn for a pleasant scent and a stronger impression in person.

quick.overview:
Perfume is a blend of aroma compounds, fixatives and a solvent, usually ethanol, worn on skin or clothing. 'Cologne' originally meant the citrus-based eau de Cologne first sold in Cologne, Germany in 1709, and in American English it usually means a men's fragrance. People wear it for a pleasant scent and a better impression on those close to them.

On looksmaxxing forums fragrance is treated as a low-effort add-on to grooming, with members ranking popular bottles. The scent is smelled by others, and no study in the sources reviewed tests whether wearing cologne changes perceived attractiveness.
quick.how: People spray or dab it on the neck, wrists or clothing after showering, choosing a strength for the occasion. Fragrances evaporate in stages, with top notes disappearing first and base notes lasting longest; Wikipedia lists parfum at about 15-30% aromatic compounds, eau de parfum at 15-20%, eau de toilette at 5-15% and eau de cologne at 2-3%, with brands varying.
quick.risks: Fragrance ingredients can cause contact dermatitis, headaches or asthma symptoms in sensitive people, and patch testing with fragrance mix gives a positive reaction in about 10% of people with eczema, according to Wikipedia. A 2020 review of essential oils, which are common in fragrance, also describes adverse effects including endocrine-disrupting properties for some oils.

angle.text: Cologne adds a pleasant scent around you, which people use to leave a better impression up close. It is a popular grooming step; trials of its effect on perceived attractiveness were not found.

rhinoplasty.summary: Surgery that reshapes the nose for looks or breathing, the most discussed facial harmony operation, with a documented revision rate and a long swelling period.

quick.overview:
Rhinoplasty is plastic surgery that changes the shape, size or proportions of the nose, or improves breathing. People seek it to reduce a dorsal hump, narrow the nostrils or tip, or change the nasolabial angle, and in looksmaxxing communities the nose is treated as a central feature of facial harmony. It is also done for functional reasons and for reconstruction after injury, birth defects or cancer.

Surgeons reshape the nasal bones and cartilages, adding, removing or repositioning tissue, sometimes with cartilage grafted from the septum, ear or rib. Published sources describe a long-established operation with high reported satisfaction in several studies.
quick.how: Surgery is done by a plastic or facial plastic surgeon, through incisions inside the nose (closed) or with an added incision across the columella (open). Preservation techniques try to keep the existing dorsum rather than cutting it down. Swelling settles gradually, and the final shape is judged after up to a year.
quick.risks: Reported complications include breathing impairment, asymmetry, collapse of tip support and prolonged swelling that can take up to a year to resolve; smoking impairs healing. Revision surgery is needed in roughly 5-20% of operations and is technically harder. Body dysmorphic disorder is more common among cosmetic surgery patients and is associated with dissatisfaction, which is why screening is recommended.

angle.text: Rhinoplasty reshapes the nose, and the change in size and proportions is visible and measurable after healing. It is discussed as the main facial-harmony operation; the idea that nose changes shift the look of the whole face is forum opinion.

bimaxillary-osteotomy-bimax.summary: Double-jaw surgery that repositions both upper and lower jaw, used for bite and airway problems and sought for a more forward, balanced facial skeleton.

quick.overview:
Bimaxillary osteotomy, or bimax, is an operation in which a surgeon cuts both the upper jaw (maxilla) and lower jaw (mandible) through the mouth, moves them to a new position and fixes them with plates and screws. Clinically it is used for bite problems such as underbites and overbites, jaw-joint problems and obstructive sleep apnoea, and in looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as the route to a stronger profile and jawline, often with counter-clockwise rotation of the jaws.

Bone cuts allow the maxilla (typically a Le Fort I osteotomy) and mandible (typically a bilateral sagittal split osteotomy) to be moved forward, back, up, down or rotated. Published research supports it for bite and airway outcomes and reports high patient satisfaction with appearance; formal evidence on purely cosmetic results is limited.
quick.how: Braces usually align the teeth for months before surgery and again afterward, and 3D virtual planning is increasingly used to plan the movements. Surgery is performed under general anaesthesia by an oral and maxillofacial surgeon, followed by months of recovery.
quick.risks: Reported risks include bleeding, swelling, infection, temporary or permanent numbness of the lip and chin, temporomandibular joint problems, condylar resorption, relapse of the jaw position and months of recovery and orthodontics. It is regulated as ordinary surgery in most countries, and cosmetic-only indications are judged case by case by surgeons.

angle.text: Bimax repositions both jaws, changing facial proportions, bite and airway, with visible skeletal change after healing. The operation is established for bite and airway problems; the cosmetic results forums describe vary by case.

lefort-1-maxillary-advancement.summary: Upper-jaw surgery that cuts and moves the maxilla forward to add midface projection, standard for bite and cleft cases.

quick.overview:
A Le Fort I osteotomy is a horizontal cut through the upper jaw, made from inside the mouth, that lets the surgeon move the maxilla forward, back, up or down and fix it with plates. Looksmaxxing forums discuss it as a way to project the midface, support the area under the eyes and correct underbites, often paired with a lower-jaw operation.

The cut passes above the tooth roots and below the cheekbone and eye socket, freeing the tooth-bearing maxilla to be repositioned in three dimensions. Clinically it is used for bite problems, a recessed or vertically long upper jaw, cleft-related underdevelopment and, with lower-jaw surgery, sleep apnoea. Published studies document stability and outcomes in functional and cleft patients; there is little research on cosmetic-only advancement.
quick.how: Plates and screws hold the new position while bone heals, and orthodontics aligns the teeth around the operation. Surgery is done by oral and maxillofacial or craniofacial surgeons under general anaesthesia, with a months-long recovery. Forum members describe advancements of several millimetres and combination with lower-jaw surgery.
quick.risks: Documented concerns include bleeding, swelling, infection, nerve numbness, relapse of the new position (greater for some movement directions and large advancements), nasal and lip changes and a months-long recovery. It is regulated as routine surgery.

angle.text: LeFort 1 moves the upper jaw forward to add midface projection, with the bone movement visible and measurable. The operation is standard for bite problems; claims of under-eye support rest mostly on bite and cleft research.
